The invention provides a system, server, method, and program for delivering information that closely matches a user’s actual interests by collecting information from sources that the user considers valuable or reliable. By reflecting both the user’s instructions and the characteristics of relevant content, the invention makes it possible to supply information that is more appropriate to the user’s needs than information obtained through a general-purpose search or a fixed recommendation process.

In this system, user instruction information is accepted from the user. The user instruction information may include, for example, a request, preference, selection, search condition, or other indication of the kind of information the user wishes to receive. In response to this instruction, the system acquires content-related information. The content-related information may include information concerning documents, articles, web pages, media content, products, topics, keywords, metadata, or other content that is relevant to the user’s instruction or interests.

The system then extracts or determines characteristic information from the acquired content-related information. Such characteristic information may represent features, keywords, topics, categories, names, trends, metadata, or other elements that characterize the content. Based on this characteristic information, the system generates one or more search queries. The generated search queries are associated with attribute information, such as information indicating the type, category, priority, source, relevance, user preference, or other attribute of the query or the content from which the query was generated.

When the user issues the instruction, the system uses the generated search queries to acquire related information. Because the related information is obtained at or near the time the instruction is issued, the system can retrieve timely and relevant information corresponding to the user’s current interests. The related information may be acquired from various information sources, including databases, websites, news sources, social media, information distribution services, or other content repositories.

After acquiring the related information, the system classifies the information into groups. Each group is assigned a weight based on factors such as relevance to the user instruction, correspondence with the characteristic information, reliability or value of the information source, freshness, frequency of occurrence, or other attribute information. The system then arranges or lists the related information according to the assigned weights, so that information considered more important, relevant, or valuable to the user is presented with higher priority.

The resulting information is then supplied to the user in a structured form, such as a ranked list, categorized display, notification, report, feed, or other user interface. In this way, the invention enables the user to receive information that reflects the user’s actual interests, is obtained from valued sources, and is organized according to relevance or importance.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a technique for providing information that more accurately reflects a user’s actual interests and preferences. In conventional information retrieval systems, information is often presented based only on a keyword entered by the user or on general search conditions. As a result, the user may receive a large amount of information that is only loosely related to the user’s true interests, or information from sources that the user does not particularly value. This makes it difficult for the user to efficiently obtain useful and meaningful information.

To address this problem, the invention generates a search query using characteristic information associated with content that is relevant to the user. The characteristic information may include, for example, keywords, categories, metadata, viewing history, usage history, evaluation information, source information, or other features extracted from or associated with content. When the user gives an instruction to obtain related information, the system uses this characteristic information to automatically generate an appropriate search query. The system then retrieves information related to the content from one or more information sources, such as databases, servers, websites, news services, document repositories, or other network-accessible resources.

The retrieved information is not merely presented in the order in which it is found. Instead, the system analyzes and classifies the retrieved information into a plurality of interest groups. Each interest group corresponds to a particular area, topic, category, preference, or degree of relevance to the user. The system assigns weights to these interest groups based on factors such as the user’s past behavior, the importance of the source, the similarity between the retrieved information and the characteristic information, the frequency of related terms, user-designated preferences, or other indicators of interest. These weights represent the degree to which each group is expected to match the user’s actual interests.

After classification and weighting, the system presents the retrieved information to the user according to the assigned weights. Information belonging to highly weighted interest groups may be displayed more prominently, ranked higher, emphasized visually, or otherwise prioritized. Information belonging to lower-weighted groups may be displayed later, grouped separately, or omitted depending on the user’s settings or system configuration. In this way, the user can quickly access information that is likely to be most relevant and valuable.

By generating search queries from content-related characteristic information at the time of a user instruction, and by classifying and weighting the retrieved information according to user interests, the invention enables more personalized and efficient information delivery. The invention reduces the burden on the user to manually formulate search queries and filter search results, while improving the likelihood that the presented information will come from sources and topics that the user values. As a result, the system can provide information that is better aligned with the user’s actual needs, interests, and priorities.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it helps us refer to something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

This simple word gives sentences clarity and direction. It helps identify people, places, objects, and ideas. Phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” and “the future” feel familiar because “the” points to something known or unique. Without it, English would sound less natural and less precise.

Although “the” may seem unimportant because it is so short, it is essential in everyday speech and writing. It connects meaning, creates focus, and helps readers and listeners understand exactly what is being discussed. In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have great power.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an information providing system that learns a user’s interests from content-related information, generates search queries, groups related information, weights the groups, and presents ranked results to the user.
counterfactuals.output: An information providing system includes one or more processors configured to acquire content-related information associated with content accessed by a user, extract feature information indicative of interests of the user, and generate one or more search queries based on the extracted feature information. The system obtains search results corresponding to the generated queries and groups information items included in the search results according to similarity, relevance, or a predetermined classification criterion. A weighting unit assigns weights to respective groups based on at least one of correspondence to the user’s interests, frequency of occurrence of related features, recency, user behavior history, or reliability of information sources. A presentation unit ranks the groups and/or information items in accordance with the assigned weights and presents the ranked results to the user through a user interface. The system thereby provides information adapted to inferred user interests while organizing related information for efficient review.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for an invention titled “Information Providing System, Information Providing Server, Information Providing Method, and Program” that retrieves information from user-valued sources based on instruction timing and interest modeling.
counterfactuals.output: An information providing system includes an information providing server configured to provide information to a user terminal based on both timing of a user instruction and a degree of user interest. The server acquires, from the user terminal, instruction information indicating a request or operation performed by a user, identifies a timing associated with the instruction information, and estimates an interest model representing interests of the user based on user behavior, user-designated preferences, past information selection history, or evaluation of information sources. The server selects one or more information sources having a value to the user in accordance with the interest model, retrieves information from the selected information sources based on the identified timing, and transmits the retrieved information to the user terminal. The information may be prioritized, filtered, or ranked according to relevance to the estimated user interest and reliability or importance of the information source. Accordingly, information that is likely to be useful to the user can be provided at an appropriate timing from sources regarded as valuable by the user.

counterfactuals.output: A system is provided for generating ranked content recommendations in response to user instructions. The system includes one or more processors and memory storing executable instructions that, when executed, cause the system to receive an instruction from a user, obtain content-related data associated with the instruction, and extract characteristic information from the content-related data, the characteristic information including one or more attributes, keywords, metadata elements, semantic features, contextual indicators, or user preference parameters. Based at least in part on the characteristic information, the system automatically generates one or more search queries and submits the search queries to one or more information sources to acquire related information. The acquired related information is analyzed and classified into a plurality of groups according to relevance, topic, source, semantic similarity, user context, or other classification criteria. counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention of an AI-based information recommendation system in formal patent language, including components for instruction acceptance, query generation, related information acquisition, interest area modeling, interest information listing, and supplying listing information.
counterfactuals.output:
An AI-based information recommendation system is provided for identifying and presenting information relevant to a user’s interests. The system comprises an instruction acceptance unit configured to receive, from a user or terminal device, an instruction requesting acquisition or recommendation of information. A query generation unit generates one or more search queries based on the accepted instruction, user input, contextual information, or previously acquired user-related data. A related information acquisition unit uses the generated query to acquire related information from one or more information sources, including databases, networks, web resources, document repositories, or external services.

The system further comprises an interest area modeling unit configured to analyze the acquired related information and generate or update an interest area model representing one or more fields, topics, categories, keywords, entities, or semantic concepts corresponding to the user’s presumed or expressed interests. An interest information listing unit extracts, ranks, classifies, or otherwise organizes information items associated with the modeled interest area and generates an interest information list. A listing information supplying unit supplies the generated list, or information derived therefrom, to the user terminal, application, or another system for display, notification, storage, or further processing.

The invention enables automatic generation of recommendation candidates by transforming a user instruction into search queries, acquiring related information, modeling an interest area based on the acquired information, and providing a structured listing of interest information, thereby improving the relevance and efficiency of information recommendation.
